candidates.title: Why an airship was spotted hovering over this central Alberta town
candidates.description: A rare sight in the sky over central Alberta last week turned heads and had people asking: Was that really a 20-metre blimp? While many have seen a Goodyear Blimp at a sporting event, it’s not every day you see such a sight in rural Alberta.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Windsor residents react to thank you banner from Detroit on Thanksgiving
candidates.description: A banner was flown above the Detroit River on Monday to thank Canadians during Thanksgiving. The initiative was organized by groups in Detroit, who wanted to commemorate the unique relationship between Windsor and the American city.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Indigenous groups criticize Wab Kinew for saying residential school denialism shouldn't be illegal
candidates.description: Leaders of Indigenous groups are speaking out against Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew's recent comments that residential school denialism should not be considered a crime.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sask. farmer trying to sell or donate town's grain elevator to avoid demolition
candidates.description: Another small Saskatchewan town's classic symbol of prairie life is in peril, but the owners are doing what they can to keep it standing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. man reunited with beloved flute, 5 years after it floated away down a Yukon river
candidates.description: Jun Takahashi was stunned when he saw the online post: someone in the Yukon bush had found a canoe barrel full of his mildew-y camping gear, and his long-lost flute.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Economic frustration helps fuel Alberta separatism — and these 4 charts suggest why
candidates.description: Alberta is a wealthy province. Yet economic frustration is part of what's driving the separation movement. But would independence improve Alberta's fortunes or bring new economic concerns?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How a loophole in Canada's species-at-risk law can leave wildlife in limbo
candidates.description: A new study finds a legal gap in Canada's Species at Risk Act can leave species waiting years for protection, with 153 of 288 cases overdue and still unresolved as of January 2025.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Coming closure of another Winnipeg Giant Tiger store will mean 'less food in the fridge,' shopper says
candidates.description: Winnipeg shoppers weren't too happy to hear that another Giant Tiger store is closing, saying it will be one less option to buy affordable groceries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cleveland-Cliffs CEO says he's prepared to fight Canada in court over Stelco layoffs
candidates.description: The CEO of the American company that owns Hamilton-based steelmaker Stelco says he's prepared to fight the Canadian government in court over Stelco's plan to lay off hundreds of workers. He also said he's open to selling the company and voiced support for U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel, despite citing tariffs as a reason for the company's economic struggles.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Support floods in for Gus, Halifax's 104-year-old gopher tortoise, ahead of surgery
candidates.description: Hundreds of get-well messages and art pieces have been sent to the tortoise before he undergoes a bladder surgery on Tuesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Disrespect for wildlife': Multiple grizzly bear poaching incidents under investigation in Alberta
candidates.description: Provincial officials are investigating the illegal killings of four grizzly bears at three separate locations over the last year. One of the bear corpses was found abandoned with its paws removed after being poached.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After 20 years as a P.E.I. firefighter, something snapped. Now he's teaching others about PTSD
candidates.description: Ernie Gallant was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder after dedicating two decades of volunteer service to the New Glasgow Fire Department in Prince Edward Island.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Zelenskyy says Russia violating Trump's 'energy ceasefire' as attacks on Ukraine continue
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says "energy ceasefire" announced by U.S. President Donald Trump can be "a major step toward ending ​the war if the Americans truly step in now." The Kremlin says contacts are ongoing about the possible "energy ceasefire."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How the ICE surge in Minnesota could impact the midterms
candidates.description: Operation Metro Surge is still a "fresh wound" in Minnesota, where a sweeping immigration crackdown saw thousands of arrested and two U.S. citizens killed. Minnesotans organized grassroots opposition against the federal officers. Now many of those same people have signed up for training to protect the polls in a Senate race that could be pivotal.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'We can’t deal with it in Canada': Some women turn to Mexico for endometriosis care
candidates.description: While endometriosis affects one in 10 women, Canada’s health care system is doing a “poor” job in providing them care and many women are seeking treatment outside the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nobel memorial prize in economics awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford
candidates.description: American-born economists' models have helped governments and central banks manage economic shocks and "smooth out the economy's peaks and troughs," says Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How did Spain's housing crisis get so bad it forced the PM to call a snap election?
candidates.description: By making housing affordability the centrepiece of his campaign, Pedro Sánchez hopes to unite progressive voters while deflecting attention from other pressing political vulnerabilities.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saudis say Riyadh airport struck for 2nd day in a row, separate airport also attacked
candidates.description: Saudi authorities said Sunday that King Fahd International Airport in Dammam has been attacked, with few details. The statement came hours after authorities said the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, had been attacked once again.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'You're Russian now': Ukrainians raised in Crimea share how Russia trained them to become future soldiers
candidates.description: Three Ukrainians who grew up in occupied Crimea describe how Russia trained them to become future soldiers for its war on Ukraine, including school classes on how to handle weapons — part of a larger pattern of Russian indoctrination of children that has raised alarm in the international community.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rescue helicopters race to flood-hit Nepal villages as 5 reported missing
candidates.description: Rescuers from Nepal's military on Monday reached an area hit by a flash flood the previous day. Five people have been reported missing and no fatalities have been reported so far.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge orders Trump administration to end taxpayer-funded TV ads
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump must cancel any remaining television commercials paid for with millions of dollars in taxpayer money to promote his political message, a federal judge ordered Sunday night, even as the administration said the ad campaign was coming to an end.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Children among at least 139 dead after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti coast
candidates.description: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a boat carrying more than 300 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti in East Africa, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hurricane Simon hits Mexico's Pacific coast, slamming towns and resorts
candidates.description: Hurricane Simon was pounding Mexico's Pacific coast as a Category 4 storm on Sunday, its eye remaining just offshore as its most powerful winds and rain slammed people living between the Sierra Madre and the ocean.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire,' which Zelenskyy says he hasn't seen but supports
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he has discussed the possibility of an energy ceasefire with Russia with Prime Minister Mark Carney, Finnish President Alex Stubb and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte but is waiting for more information from the United States.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pope Leo will undergo surgery to remove a nodule on his lung
candidates.description: Pope Leo announced Sunday he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a nodular lesion on his lung that was recently discovered during medical checks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What happens when a Google data centre comes to town? Southern India is finding out
candidates.description: India is vying to secure a piece of the AI boom, and letting Google clear hundreds of acres to build a $15 billion US data centre hub near its eastern coast. It will be the company's largest such project outside the U.S., and comes with promises of jobs and investments. But at what cost?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Panama declares state of emergency as powerful quake aftershocks rattle communities
candidates.description: The government of Panama declared a state of emergency Saturday as the aftershocks of two powerful earthquakes that roiled the country shook communities for hours. Officials did not attribute any deaths to the quakes but reported damages in all 10 of Panama's provinces and two Indigenous territories.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Villages evacuated as flash flood from Budhi Gandaki river hits northern Nepal
candidates.description: Residents along the Budhi Gandaki river in north central Nepal evacuated on Sunday as flash flooding destroyed homes and other structures in the area.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why Moscow is staying tight-lipped on Trump's energy ceasefire
candidates.description: While Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky suggests he would sign up to a ceasefire on energy infrastructure, Russia has said little.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
candidates.description: It comes after the armed group hit Riyadh's international airport and another facility, killing 13 people, in a significant escalation.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Immigration agents search congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
candidates.description: Omar, an outspoken Trump critic, said the search was "an attempt to target political enemies" and she "will not be silenced".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
candidates.description: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak
candidates.description: The flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled after passengers on the plane's previous journey complained of bug bites.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Tom Cruise film Digger forecast to become one of Hollywood's biggest flops
candidates.description: The film dropped by around 60% in its second weekend, and could become one of Hollywood's biggest flops.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia
candidates.description: Both Republican and Democratic lawmakers have criticised the deal, which was announced weeks before the US midterm elections.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at ex-PM's national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
candidates.description: After analysing 1,500 videos and images of the Raila Odinga memorial, Africa Eye finds that those killed were far from the scuffles.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Women's billion-dollar boom leaves players behind, says Fifpro
candidates.description: Women's football is on course to become a billion-dollar industry, but many professional players are still earning low wages, working on insecure contracts and experiencing rising psychological stress, a Fifpro survey indicates.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
candidates.description: The PM was speaking after violent attacks at Polish schools this week left one dead and others injured.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
candidates.description: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
candidates.description: It is the third time this week that Ukraine has targeted Russian tech giant Yandex, forcing the company to suspend its operations.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why the US is bringing back firing squads
candidates.description: The execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan would be the first time the US Army had used a firing squad since 1945.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: American ranchers wrestle with soaring costs - and their loyalty to Trump
candidates.description: Many farmers in states that backed the president say they are being hit from all sides, with the crucial midterm elections just weeks away.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Robert Pattinson on new film Primetime and how hunting predators became hit TV
candidates.description: The actor portrays the real-life host of American TV show, To Catch a Predator, in his latest film.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Riyadh airport attacks another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
candidates.description: While the physical damage from Houthi attacks can be quickly repaired, the Saudi reputation for stability is taking a battering.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why is it so hard to fight the Houthis?
candidates.description: Security correspondent Frank Gardner explains how the Iran-backed Houthis' precision strikes and guerrilla tactics have made it difficult for Saudi forces to gain the upper hand.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
candidates.description: Brad Smith calls for global rules on AI, and says the UK is in the "best position" to lead the charge.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Crew searching for Amelia Earhart arrives at crab-infested island
candidates.description: Researchers will sleep on their ship to avoid giant crabs that can lift heavy weights, split open coconuts, and may have played a role in Earhart's demise.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Storm Rachel batters Southern California, brings flooding to Las Vegas
candidates.description: Large waves from the post-tropical cyclone battered homes in Long Beach, and brought flooding to parts of Las Vegas near the famed Strip.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
candidates.description: Roofs were ripped off buildings after Isaias barrelled into the US on Friday evening, before it weakened to a post-tropical cyclone.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Stinky 'skunk' plant cleared from river
candidates.description: The plant is said to smell like "rotting meat" and is is native to swamps and other wetlands in the Pacific Northwest.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump announced a partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Did either country know about it?
candidates.description: Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack Ukraine and is ignoring an "energy ceasefire" declared by President Trump.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Many Iranians who go to Turkey to find jobs are exploited
candidates.description: Desperate Iranians are finding work in Turkey to make ends meet, but many are being exploited and left with nothing but more debt.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Both Russia and Ukraine are using AI-powered drones on the battlefield
candidates.description: A Ukrainian company that got rich making smartphone-controlled cameras to watch pets at home now outfits first-person-view drones with an image recognition system powered by artificial intelligence.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: India's opposition parties march to top court as protests over voter lists escalate
candidates.description: Opposition parties say revisions to the list of eligible voters favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party. Authorities have removed more than 130 million names from the voter roll.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: DOJ launches antitrust probe of TV networks. And, Trump says Ukraine needs new leader
candidates.description: The Justice Department is investigating several TV networks for possible antitrust violations. And, President Trump pressures Ukrainians to elect a new leader.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russia hits Ukraine gas facilities after Trump claims 'energy ceasefire'
candidates.description: Trump said he had brokered a cease-fire to protect energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine. But Ukrainian officials say bombs kept falling overnight on gas facilities, wounding 33 people.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Seafarer's union official says crews offered big money to transit Strait of Hormuz
candidates.description: As attacks continue to mount on shipping vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a seafarer's union official says some crews are being offered big rewards for making the crossing.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Harrowing accounts of violence and sex abuse in women's prison told in new podcast
candidates.description: Madi Bolanos and Anna Sussman's new podcast We Are Jane Doe, by KQED and Snap Studios, investigates rampant sex abuse at the Central California Women's Facility in Chowchilla, Ca.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ukrainian MP calls U.S.-Russia diesel deal a 'betrayal'
candidates.description: NPR's Joel Rose speaks with Ukrainian Minister of Parliament, Oleksandr Merezhko, about the U.S.'s diesel deal with Russia will impact Ukraine.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Farmers say they'll take the relief of Trump's EO — but they're still hurting
candidates.description: President Trump says his Monday executive order temporarily suspending federal taxes on diesel will be a big relief for farmers. Some farmers call it a campaign ploy with marginal impact.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 2 Americans win Nobel Prize in economics for work on boom-bust cycles
candidates.description: Two Americans have won the Nobel Prize in economics for their work on how to smooth boom-and-bust cycles to limit unemployment and inflation.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Justice Department investigates TV networks, citing possible anti-trust violations
candidates.description: The move escalates Trump's fight with the press amid court battle over barring CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: It's taking longer to find a new job after losing one
candidates.description: People who lose their jobs in this economy are taking longer to find new work. Nearly four in ten people exhaust their unemployment benefits before they land a new job.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Rise in accidents involving kids and e-bikes sparks debate about regulation
candidates.description: Emergency room departments are reporting soaring numbers of pediatric trauma accidents associated with micromobility devices. Experts and advocates agree that the federal government needs to step in.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Sauna research gathers steam
candidates.description: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Here's what to know if you're unsure about your measles immunity status
candidates.description: Vaccination is the best way to protect yourself against measles. For most adults, one shot of the MMR is considered enough protection. But there are certain situations that call for a second dose.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
candidates.description: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
candidates.description: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
candidates.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
candidates.description: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.
candidates.author: NPR
